To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the palladium complexes of phosphinothioethers are highly effective catalysts in Suzuki coupling reactions and are able to catalyze the reaction in high turnover numbers, up to 200 0000, and that the reaction rate is linearly dependent on the catalyst concentration.

we have synthesized and structurally characterized benzyl phosphino thioether and thiolato PdII complexes and have shown that the former complexes can catalyse the Suzuki reaction at very high turnover numbers.
The synthesis of the phosphino-thioethers Ph(2) PCH(2) CH(Et) SR, R = CH2 Ph, R = CH 2 3, 5-Me-C6H3 and R = 3,5-(MeO) 2-C6H3, is reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new phosphine ligands and their corresponding Pd(II)-complexes and their applications in catalytic reactions, especially in Suzuki cross-coupling.
the synthesis of new ligands and their application to the synthesis of palladium complexes.
the development of new phosphine ligands and their palladium complexes as catalyst precursors for the Suzuki cross-coupling of aryl bromides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phosphinothiolate ligand is superior to the phosphinothiether ligand in terms of catalytic activity in the Suzuki reaction, and that the activity of the phosphino ligand is surpassed by that of the phosphino-thiols in the Suzuki cross-coupling of aryl bromides.
the phosphinothiolates are better catalysts than the phosphinothiethers, but that the latter are better than the parent phosphino ligands, with the thiolates being the best catalysts of all.
the phosphinothiolates perform better than the phosphinothiophosphonates and the phosphinothiomethylphosphonates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phosphino-thioethers are better than the phosphino-thiolates as ligands for palladium, and that the benzyl phosphine-thioether ligands are better than the corresponding alkyl phosphine-thiolate ligands.
the phosphinothiolate ligand is the superior catalyst, but the phosphinothiether is the superior catalyst precursor.
the phosphinothiol ligand Ph(3)PCH(3)S(-) is a very effective catalyst for Suzuki coupling reactions, with turnover numbers up to the millions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the benzylphosphinothioethers as ligands in palladium catalysed cross-coupling chemistry is a promising new approach.
the phosphinothiolates are better ligands for the Pd-catalysed cross-coupling of aryl halides with arylboronic acids than the corresponding thioethers.

the phosphinothiols are excellent ligands for Pd(II)-catalysed C-C coupling reactions, and that the corresponding phosphinothioethers, which are readily available from the parent thiols, are also effective ligands for P(II).
